data.ruling:
The refutation does not hold, and the RP2354B stays. The stock verifier refutes nothing: its verdict is 'incomplete', its refutation text is empty, and all 14 of its checks pass. The datasheet verifier fails 3 checks: 'watchdog stop deadline (V1)', 'watchdog stall cover (V2)' and 'watchdog window (V1 and V2)'. None of the 3 is a property of the part.

(1) V1, the stop deadline. The part sets any watchdog LOAD up to 0xffffff us, which is 16,777,215 us or about 16.8 s (Table 1249, re-read). V1 is marked 'for research' (Research.md:561), and FU-A2 adjudicator-R1-2 ruled it not found. IOBoard.md:221 still says 'The watchdog timeout and the stop deadline it serves are not stated'. A timeout cannot fail a deadline that has no value, and the verifier itself says 'Not a property of the part'.

(2) V2, the longest legitimate stall. I re-read pico-sdk 2.3.1 stdio_usb_out_chars(). It sets last_avail_time after every accepted chunk. It leaves the loop early only when no space is free and more than PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US (500,000 us by default) has passed since the last accepted chunk. Otherwise it runs until all 'length' bytes are written. So when a host keeps accepting data slowly, the stall is limited only by the message length and the host's rate. No fixed bound exists. That stall comes from the firmware and the host. The microcontroller does not set it, and no watchdog on any part covers a stall with no bound. Firmware/ in checkout e13f5f60 has no watchdog_enable, no watchdog_update and no override of PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US, so the finding still describes the code. The part can set a timeout above the finite cases the verifier names, 800 ms and 900 ms.

(3) The window. It depends on V1 and V2, so it cannot be decided while V1 is not found and V2 has no bound. That is an open question for the owner, not a limit of the silicon.

The RP2354B is also a fixed input. Research.md Scope (lines 42-43) says fixed inputs are checked for stock, lifecycle and a second source, and a fixed input that fails a check is reported to the owner, not re-selected.

I re-read the part-level facts, and every one passes:
- JLCPCB lists C39843328 as RP2354B, Raspberry Pi, QFN-80-EP(10x10), erpComponentName SC1512(13)-A4, with stock 2972 and presale 2815. Both are above the gate of 50 and above 0.
- The 20 held parts cover the need of 5 boards x 1 = 5.
- Digi-Key lists SC1512(13)-A4 with 3560 in stock, end_of_life false and discontinued false.
- The PCN (product change notice) listing still holds only the RP235x A4 stepping PCN. That notice ends the steppings other than A4, and C39843328 is the A4 part.
- The maker, Raspberry Pi, is on the S1 allowlist.

Two things go to the owner and to P5 as findings: V1 is not found, and V2 has no bound under the slow-host case. Q8, moving the store off the flash, and a lower console timeout would each change V2. This ruling matches FU-A2 adjudicator-R1 (022). The scope is function, because all three failed rows are about this function's requirement values (V1, V2, V4). None is about lifecycle, an end-of-life notice, the maker allowlist or the LCSC identity.
